lines.text: This man checks into Room 305 every Friday night.
And every night, at exactly 1:12, he picks up the phone and calls the room next door.
He doesn't say a word. He hangs up, and two minutes later he's fast asleep.
Nadia, the night receptionist, sees it light up her switchboard every single Friday, and it's driving her crazy.
Then one Friday, Room 306 is empty, and something strange happens.
At 1:12, he's wide awake in the same bed.
But this time, no call. He just rolls over and sleeps.
Nadia checks the phone. It works fine, and no other guest does this.
So why does he only call when someone is in 306?
You have ten seconds. Comment your answer now.
Time's up.
One Friday, Nadia takes a late tea up to the third floor, and she hears it right through the wall.
Room 306 snores.
Not a little. Like a chainsaw.
The man in 305 can't sleep through that, so at 1:12 he dials 306.
The phone rings. The snorer wakes up and says, hello?
Silence. Click.
Now 306 lies awake, wondering who called, and for two quiet minutes, nobody snores.
That's all 305 needs.
Nadia laughs so hard she drops her pen.
Next Friday, she gives 305 a room on the top floor, and the switchboard stays dark.
So, did you get it right? Follow for more.
